speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for over three weeks now. It's mostly dry, but sometimes I cough up a little white phlegm, and I've noticed I get quite short of breath when I try to walk or do any physical activity. However, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing the CT results; the bilateral ground-glass opacities are significant. Have you recently traveled, been around anyone with a fever, or had any contact with someone who was sick? Also, do you have any history of autoimmune diseases or recent viral infections?

text: No, I haven't traveled recently or been around anyone sick, and I don't have any history of autoimmune diseases. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the CT findings and your history. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis (likely due to environmental antigen exposure such as mold or bird droppings).
